newsitem.title: DUBAI: GCC chief arrives in Oman to prepare for summit.
newsitem.headline: GCC chief arrives in Oman to prepare for summit.

text.p: The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) arrived in Oman on Sunday as part of a regional tour to prepare for the next Gulf Arab summit in Qatar.
GCC Secretary-General Jameel Hujilan, who flew in from Doha, told Oman's state-run news agency he would meet Sultan Qaboos bin Said to hear his views on the planned summit.
Earlier in the day, Qatari newspapers quoted him as saying the meeting was set for December 7.

Hujilan's tour comes amid border rows and differences within the alliance, which also groups Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates. Hujilan was going on to the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, GCC officials said.

Hujilan, trying to persuade Bahrain's ruler to attend the summit, visited Manama last Monday. Diplomats said he feared Manama's absence from the meeting, expected to prove a watershed in the history of the GCC, would set a precedent.

Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a territorial dispute over a cluster of barren reefs and islands that are potentially rich in oil and gas. They include Hawar islands, controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.

Bahrain has threatened to boycott the summit because of Qatar's failure to withdraw the case from the International Court of Justice. Qatar asked the court in 1991 to settle the dispute and a verdict is expected by the end of this year.
Qatar said it would only withdraw the case from the world court in the Hague if Saudi Arabia's mediation succeeded in settling the long-standing border row.

While in Muscat, Hujilan was expected to attend a meeting of GCC justice ministers seeking ways to combat terrorism and ease travel restrictions among member states, local newspapers said. The meeting was due to open on Monday.
